hook-hub.slice: hook-hub internals end to end for claude and codex: bb-hook client, hub.py dispatch, handler rows, recorder tap points, native event inventory
hook-hub.summary: Every native hook event from Claude Code and Codex CLI runs ~/.agents/hooks/bb-hook, a stdlib-only client. It frames the payload as one JSON line to hook-hub over the systemd-activated unix socket /run/user/1000/33god/hook-hub.sock. The hub (asyncio daemon, hub.py) then does the following in order. 1) It reloads handlers.toml and hooks.master.json by mtime. 2) It resolves the role from the (cli,native) binding. 3) It claims an invocation_id in a SQLite receipt journal. 4) It selects handlers, skipping rows with a recorded reason. 5) It always puts the internal bloodbank-publisher first. 6) It spawns async handlers into an 8-slot pool. 7) It runs sync handlers strictly one after another under one shared deadline of min(budget_s, 14s). 8) It merges the sync handlers' JSON stdout into a single reply, and bb-hook relays that reply to the CLI. The only thing that reaches the model is additionalContext, plus exit 2 with stderr on a deny. The publisher subprocess (agent-hooks/publish.py) does these steps. 1) It feeds the Agent State Machine (ASM) in Redis. 2) It builds a CloudEvents envelope from per-session state. 3) It publishes to core NATS and treats a PONG as success. 4) Attention events go to deckard.evt.attention instead. Every receipt mutation also enqueues a coalesced hook.updated observation fact into a transactional outbox. A worker flushes that outbox to JetStream (BLOODBANK_EVENTS) with a real PubAck, and Candystore then stores it. Async handlers (Hindsight capture, Nanoleaf, Orca, jot flush, merge-forward and others) finish after the turn, and merge-forward can run up to 905s. The hub records outcomes but never stores prompt, stdout or stderr. Raw payloads and handler stdio are therefore not recorded anywhere today. Secondary evidence does exist: Claude transcript hook_success and hook_additional_context attachments, Codex rollout developer messages, Candystore events, and per-handler state files. No trace or record flag exists. The recorder needs a small opt-in tee in hub.py (dispatch, run_handler/decode_result, compose_stdout, handle_request except) and an optional trace field from bb-hook. Several silent-failure paths exist and are listed under surprises. Most are verified live.

steps.action: maybe_reload() re-reads handlers.toml and hooks.master.json by mtime (no overlay on this host). Resolves role from the (cli,native) binding. event_type is the lifecycle type, or deckard.v1.agent.attention for alert bindings. invocation_identity: if the request has no id, a native event id or tool call id gives uuid5([cli,native,session,key]) (kinds native_event/tool_call), else uuid4 'generated'. claim() is INSERT OR IGNORE into invocations; a duplicate increments `deduplicated` and short-circuits. A request without cli/native (ping) is answered immediately and not journalled.

steps.action: Sync handlers run sequentially under one shared deadline min(budget_s,14s). Per-handler timeout = min(timeout_ms, remaining). An exhausted budget gives status skipped, reason sync_budget_exhausted (seen 3x on claude hub-selftest). Handler stdin is the payload JSON. Each prints {"_hook_hub":{status,reason,exit_code},"stdout":"<native JSON>"}. Order for claude prompt: skill-reminder (0, 1000ms; runs reminder-for-skill-check.sh), crank-tag (1; skips not_a_crank_prompt unless prompt starts [crank]/[crank relay]), hindsight-recall (10, 11000ms), codegraph-prompt (20, 2000ms; effectively dead, see surprises), hub-selftest (999, `env true`, 500ms). Its skip reasons: prompt_under_min_length, query_under_min_length_after_cleanup, query_has_no_word_characters, hindsight_binary_missing, hindsight_disabled.

steps.action: decode_result strips stdout for failed or skipped results unless exit_code==2. compose_stdout merges JSON objects: additionalContext values joined with \n\n, deny outranks allow, exit 2 propagated with stderr. Reply {stdout,stderr,exit_code} is returned on the socket and bb-hook writes stdout/stderr to the CLI (exit code only 0..125 from reply). The reply is not logged or stored.

Claude wraps the injected context as {hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName,additionalContext}} and stores it in the transcript (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl) as an `attachment` of type hook_success (hookEvent, command, stdout, stderr, exitCode, durationMs) and hook_additional_context (content[]). bb-hook records appear only when it prints something (Orca prints {}). Codex stores the injected context as a response_item role=developer in ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*-<thread>.jsonl (REMINDER, AAI_ROUTE_PROOF marker).
side_effects: context becomes part of the model prompt

steps.action: receipts _enqueue stores a coalesced full-invocation projection under key invocation:<iid>. Unsettled invocations wait 2s of quiet (HOOK_HUB_OBSERVATION_DEBOUNCE), at most 10s from first change. Settled ones publish at once. Publish is NATS HPUB to the event's own subject with Nats-Msg-Id and Nats-Expected-Stream BLOODBANK_EVENTS and a JetStream PubAck check. Envelope: correlationid = stable_uuid(invocation_id), ordering_key hook:<hub>:<iid>, actor {service,hook-hub,cli}, max 900KB. Types bloodbank.agent.hook.updated and bloodbank.system.hook.updated. Also a snapshot/heartbeat every 30s and a full inventory hourly.

steps.trigger: hub down, wedged, DB locked, budget exhausted, handler timeout, duplicate
steps.action: Hub down or wedged: ping fails and bb-hook prints nothing and exits 0 (a 0.25s probe for 30s after a stall). SQLite OperationalError (timeout 2s) in claim or update: handle_request's except Exception returns an empty reply with only a log line, and execute does not catch it, so the handler never runs. Handler timeout: killpg and a failed or timed-out receipt, stdout dropped. Sync budget exhausted: sync_budget_exhausted skip. Duplicate invocation: deduplicated counter (never seen firing). recover() runs only at hub start and marks pending rows failed with hub_restarted.
side_effects: silent loss of context or receipts

evidence.locator: ~/.local/state/33god/hook-hub/hub.log

capture_recipes.command: sqlite3 -readonly ~/.local/state/33god/hook-hub/receipts.sqlite3 "select sequence,invocation_id,handler_id,status,reason,at from receipt_events where sequence>N order by sequence"
capture_recipes.yields: A live-tailable ordered stream of every handler state change (columns sequence, invocation_id, handler_id, status, reason, at). Also the invocations/executions tables.

bus.summary:
The bus is a single-node NATS 2.10.29 JetStream at 127.0.0.1:4222 (monitoring on :8222; env BLOODBANK_NATS_HOST/PORT=127.0.0.1/4222). There is no nats CLI on the host, but system python3 has `nats` (nats-py) and can issue read-only `$JS.API.*` requests. A nats-box image (natsio/nats-box:0.14.5) is also present locally. Three streams exist: BLOODBANK_EVENTS (`bloodbank.evt.>`, limits retention, 7d max_age, file storage, 120s dedupe window, allow_direct=true, 1,090,143 msgs, seq 9339214..10429356 at first read), BLOODBANK_COMMANDS (`bloodbank.cmd.>` and `bloodbank.rpy.>`, workqueue, 1d) and GIB_EVENTS (a game, excluded).

THE TURN'S PATH THROUGH THE BUS (verified live for fe69f4eb):
1. The hook-hub handler `bloodbank-publisher` (async) runs agent-hooks `publish.py`, which builds the envelope and sends it as a plain core-NATS `PUB`. There is no HPUB, no Nats-Msg-Id and no JetStream PubAck; the publisher only waits for PONG.
2. JetStream captures it as stream seq 10427983 at 03:53:25.5077Z. The envelope `time` is 25.506 and the hub receipt's publisher execution finished at 25.515.
3. Three JetStream consumers match `bloodbank.evt.conversation.turn.started`:
   - `candystore-events`: Dapr push consumer, queue group `candystore`, deliver=all, explicit ack. Candystore inserted the row with `received_at` 25.514222 (+8.2ms).
   - `enricher-events`: Dapr push consumer, queue group `enricher`, deliver=new. It receives the event and ignores it.
   - `holocene_<uuid>_1`: ordered ephemeral consumer, ack=none, by_start_sequence. It records stream sequence 10427983 and collected_at 25.508Z in `~/.local/state/holocene/events.sqlite3`, readable at `GET :4000/api/events`.
4. Core (non-JetStream) subscribers see it with no durability or ack:
   - ntfy-router, subscribed to `bloodbank.evt.>`. It logged `routed: bloodbank.conversation.turn.started` at 03:53:25,630, so each prompt posts a notification to ntfy topic `bloodbank` unless rate-limited.
   - deckard, subscribed to `conversation.turn.>` and others. It updates Stream Deck tiles.
   - turn-enricher, subscribed only to `turn.completed`.

CAUSATION CHAIN (verified in Postgres for the session):
- `agent.session.started` has id = correlationid = causationid = the native Claude session UUID.
- Every later event's `causationid` is the id of the previous event the hub published for that session (`SessionState.last_event_id`). This is a linear chain per session, not a tree. `turn.started.causationid` is the session id. The first `tool.requested` points at `turn.started`, and each `tool.completed` points at its `tool.requested`.
- `turn.completed` (c35087c2) was followed 331ms later by turn-enricher's `turn.annotated` (30f1eb8a), with causationid = the turn.completed id, correlationid preserved, and ordering_key = `<source id>.annotated`.

OTHER FACTS FOR THE RECORDER:
- hook-hub mirrors its own receipts to the bus as `bloodbank.agent.hook.updated` through a real JetStream HPUB (Nats-Msg-Id and Nats-Expected-Stream, PubAck-confirmed, retried from an outbox). Their correlationid is the hook invocation_id, not the session. So the receipt for the prompt (invocation bdbdba89, stream seq 10427985, Candystore row at 03:53:26.18) is findable by `correlationid=<invocation_id>`. ASM transition invocations produce about 6,000 of these per hour.
- Model-call evidence is `bloodbank.llm.usage.recorded` and `llm.allowance.observed`, produced by aai-llm-observability (producer `automaticai-usage-exporter`) from gateway logs. They carry `data.session_id`, route, token usage, latency and request_id. Their correlationid is their own id and they are not in `/sessions/{id}`. Candystore's `q` and `correlationid` filters cannot find them (both returned 0 for this session). Only SQL on `data->>'session_id'` (254 rows in 30 min) or the Holocene store can.
- Candystore exposes event time (`time`) but not ingest time. `received_at DEFAULT NOW()` exists in Postgres but no HTTP endpoint returns it.
- Apicurio is not running, so `apicurio://holyfields/<type>/versions/1` cannot be dereferenced. Schemas live as files in `bloodbank/schemas/bloodbank/<domain>/<entity>.<action>.json`.
- Per-consumer ack status per seq is only available as a lower bound (`ack_floor.stream_seq >= seq`). Core-NATS consumers have no ack at all.

capture_recipes.source: NATS JetStream: fetch a message by stream sequence (python nats-py from system python3; no nats CLI on host)
capture_recipes.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import asyncio,json,base64,nats
async def main():
    nc=await nats.connect('nats://127.0.0.1:4222',name='waybill-recorder')
    r=await nc.request('$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET.BLOODBANK_EVENTS',json.dumps({'seq':10427983}).encode(),timeout=5)
    m=json.loads(r.data)['message']  # subject, seq, time, hdrs(b64), data(b64)
    # next message on a subject after a seq (allow_direct=true):
    r=await nc.request('$JS.API.DIRECT.GET.BLOODBANK_EVENTS',json.dumps({'seq':10427900,'next_by_subj':'bloodbank.evt.conversation.turn.started'}).encode(),timeout=5)
    print(r.headers['Nats-Sequence'],r.headers['Nats-Time-Stamp'],json.loads(r.data)['id'])
asyncio.run(main())
EOF
(alternative: docker run --rm --network host natsio/nats-box:0.14.5 nats --server 127.0.0.1:4222 stream get BLOODBANK_EVENTS 10427983 ; image is present locally)
capture_recipes.yields: Exact message (envelope JSON plus headers) and the JetStream store timestamp (publish-to-store latency: envelope time 25.506 -> stored 25.5077). Headers show whether Nats-Msg-Id was used. STREAM.INFO with {'subjects_filter':'bloodbank.evt.conversation.>'} returns per-subject message counts (turn.started 2934, completed 2823, annotated 2171).
capture_recipes.caveats: No lookup by event id or Nats-Msg-Id exists; find the seq through Holocene (items[].sequence) or by walking DIRECT.GET next_by_subj. 'start_time' in DIRECT.GET is ignored by 2.10.29 (it returned the oldest message), so time-based seeking needs a binary search over seq on the message time (about 20 requests). Opening a client connection is itself recorded in connz; do not create consumers (that mutates server state).

unobservable.what: Whether the bloodbank-publisher's core PUB actually reached the stream (stored) at publish time
unobservable.why: nats_publish waits only for PONG and never reads a JetStream PubAck; no Nats-Msg-Id header. If NATS accepted the connection but the stream rejected or lost the message there is no error; hub receipts still say publish_status=sent. Only a later stream lookup proves storage.
unobservable.proposed_tap: Recorder-side verify: after a turn, resolve the event id to a stream seq via Holocene /api/events and compare to the hub receipt's event_id; or change publisher to HPUB with Nats-Msg-Id and read the PubAck (as hook-hub observations.py already does).

unobservable.what: Which individual JetStream consumers acked a specific sequence
unobservable.why: Only ack_floor and num_ack_pending are exposed; there is no per-sequence ack list. A floor that lags (enricher-events floor 10429658 vs delivered 10431997 with 5 ack_pending) makes 'floor >= seq' a conservative lower bound, and core-NATS subscribers (ntfy-router, deckard, turn-enricher) have no ack concept.
unobservable.proposed_tap: Sample /jsz before and after the turn and report floor, delivered and ack_pending per matching consumer; for Candystore confirm by row presence (received_at), for Holocene by sequence in /api/events, for enricher by 'Successfully embedded' log or event_embeddings row.

unobservable.what: Per-event ntfy delivery (what was pushed to the phone and whether it was rate-limited)
unobservable.why: ntfy-router logs the event TYPE and a disposition ('routed'/'digested'/'rate-limited') but no event id, title or ntfy message id; the token-bucket drops are counted only in memory. ntfy server cache was not read (requires its token).
unobservable.proposed_tap: Add event id and ntfy message id to the router's log line, or poll ntfy's own JSON API for topic bloodbank with since= and match on title text.

unobservable.what: Deckard tile state changes and the amber/attention decision
unobservable.why: Rust daemon updates the Stream Deck in memory; journalctl --user -u deckard shows nothing for the prompt; deckard.evt.attention is a separate subject published only by the hook path.
unobservable.proposed_tap: Query the deckard loopback socket (daemon state) at turn start and end, or have deckard log (event id, activity, pane) per tile change.

unobservable.what: turn-enricher decisions (noise skip, Jev/Clairic outbound calls, extractor pauses)
unobservable.why: Noise turns publish nothing; outbound HTTPS calls to jev.delo.sh and Cloudflare are only counted in the periodic stats line; its core subscription is non-durable so a turn.completed that arrives while the container is down is lost without trace. docker logs were empty for the window.
unobservable.proposed_tap: Emit a lightweight 'turn.enrichment.skipped' event (or log line with target_event_id and reason), and log the Jev/Clairic HTTP status per turn.

unobservable.what: Enricher embedding time and failures per tool.completed
unobservable.why: event_embeddings has no timestamp column, the INSERT is idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and returns SUCCESS for ignored event types; an FK race with Candystore's insert would be retried silently. 304 rows exist for the session but there is no per-row time.
unobservable.proposed_tap: Add created_at DEFAULT now() to event_embeddings (migration) or parse the 'Successfully embedded tool event <id>' log lines with timestamps.

unobservable.what: artifact-sidecar disposition for events that do not qualify
unobservable.why: Acked with no ledger row, no log line and no event; only qualifying captures create processed_sources/outbox rows.
unobservable.proposed_tap: Count and log dispositions per source_event_id (qualified/unqualified/held/duplicate) to a small sqlite table or a bus event.

unobservable.what: n8n BloodbankTrigger filter drops
unobservable.why: Four n8n durables consume agent.invocation.* (and the 'Ticket Pickup Chip' trigger filters on data.context.reason in ticket-grooming/ticket-delegation); for an interactive Claude/Codex turn the event is delivered and silently dropped by the node filter, visible only in n8n execution logs if at all. Two n8n durables (n8n-8mmq..., n8n-l0J53...) have been unbound since 2026-11-14 and hold 1060 and 985 pending messages.
unobservable.proposed_tap: Read n8n executions API for the workflow ids filtered by time, or add a bloodbank 'consumed/filtered' counter.

unobservable.what: Dapr redelivery attempts and ack latency per event (Candystore and enricher)
unobservable.why: Dapr hides the NATS delivery count; JetStream exposes only num_redelivered per consumer (0 for both at read time); the app logs only HTTP 200/DROP/RETRY lines without event id (candystore log_message is silenced).
unobservable.proposed_tap: Poll /jsz num_redelivered and num_ack_pending; compare envelope time to received_at (the Candystore lag already visible) as the effective delivery latency.

unobservable.what: Schema validation outcome at the producer (BLOODBANK_HOOK_VALIDATE=1 is off by default)
unobservable.why: core.validate.assert_contract always runs structural checks, but full JSON-schema validation against bloodbank/schemas runs only when BLOODBANK_HOOK_VALIDATE=1 or validate=True; the registry (Apicurio) is not running, so no consumer validates data against a registered schema.
unobservable.proposed_tap: Recorder validates each captured event against the local schema file for its type and records pass/fail in the dump.

surprises: Prompt events are published with a plain core-NATS PUB (no headers, no Nats-Msg-Id, no JetStream PubAck). Only hook-hub's hook.updated mirror and artifact-sidecar's artifact.created use awaited JetStream publishes with Nats-Msg-Id. The stream's 120s dedupe window therefore protects those two but not turn.started or the tool events.

hook-hub's receipts are on the bus. bloodbank.agent.hook.updated carries the complete timeline and executions of every hook invocation (about 6,000 per hour), published with correlationid = the hook invocation_id, not the session. A recorder can get the whole hub half of the story from Candystore (events where correlationid = invocation_id), with no new tap on the hub.

The ONLY per-model-call evidence is the llm.usage.recorded / llm.allowance.observed pair, which has its own id as correlationid and links to the session only through data.session_id. The Candystore HTTP API cannot find them by session (both correlationid and q returned 0 rows), but SQL on data->>'session_id' returned 254 rows in 30 min. Claude Code traffic goes through the AutomaticAI gateway (token aai:claude-code:*).

Tool events carry data.turn_number, but it is a per-session tool counter (167 in a session with a single conversation turn), not a turn index. Only conversation.turn.* events have turn_id. Attributing tools to a prompt requires time windows or walking the causationid chain between turn.started and turn.completed.

causationid is a linear 'previous event' chain per session maintained in a state file (last_event_id), not a causal DAG: with parallel subagents their invocation.started events chain onto each other. True causation exists only for service-produced events (turn.annotated, project.artifact.created).
traceparent is useless: of 131,282 events in the last 24h, 75,485 carry the all-zero placeholder and 55,797 are NULL; none carries a real trace id. The recorder must mint its own trace id.

Every enricher session summary is thrown away: the enricher publishes report.session.completed as a plain dict via Dapr, Candystore rejects the wrapper as missing producer/service/domain/kind and DROPs it into dead_letter (158 in 24h, latest 04:00:41). The summary is recoverable only from dead_letter.raw.

ntfy-router pushes a notification for each prompt (turn.started and turn.annotated are 'route' class), subject to a token bucket; tool.* are digested every 300s; agent.hook.updated is muted. The only trace is a docker log line without an event id.

Candystore's API never returns received_at even though the column exists; 'published at X, archived at Y' needs SQL on 127.0.0.1:5434. The lag is tiny: for this session's first events 5.8-12.6ms; fleet last hour p50 20ms, p99 3.9s, max 2m10s.

Holocene already holds what a recorder needs: its sqlite read model stores stream sequence and collected_at for every event, with a live SSE tail and cursor resume, but offers no id or correlationid filter, so locating one event means paging by cursor.

Apicurio (bb-apicurio) is not running anywhere; the envelope's dataschema apicurio://holyfields/... URIs are unresolvable labels. Authoritative schemas are the local files under bloodbank/schemas/bloodbank/<domain>/<entity>.<action>.json (JSON Schema 2020-12 over _common/cloudevent_base.v1.json). Some audio producers use https://33god.dev/schemas/... instead.

JetStream cannot look up by Nats-Msg-Id and DIRECT.GET start_time is ignored on 2.10.29; it returned the oldest message, so a time seek needs a seq binary search (works fine using seq + next_by_subj).

Three JetStream consumers match turn.started (candystore-events, enricher-events, Holocene's ordered consumer) and three core subscribers see it without any durability (ntfy-router, deckard, plus turn-enricher for turn.completed). The core ones lose events whenever they are down and leave no gap record. enricher-events ack_floor sits far behind delivered (10429658 vs 10431997, 5 ack_pending) because head-of-line messages are slow; a 'floor >= seq' test under-reports.

Two n8n durable consumers (n8n-8mmq... on repo.task.updated and n8n-l0J53... on agent.invocation.completed) have been unbound since 2026-11-14 11:46 with 1060 and 985 pending messages, quietly accumulating. A smoke-check consumer also has 28 pending. None sit on the prompt path.

Atlas component records are stale on bb-nats and bb-apicurio: bb-nats runs as docker container bloodbank-nats on 4222/8222 (matches), but its stream message counts and 'GIB excluded' note are old, and bb-apicurio is accurately 'built-not-running'. lifecycle-controller has no running unit or container and consumes nothing from the bus today.

The bus path for Codex is the same publish.py/bb-hook pipeline but data is nested under data.payload and hook, and Codex tool coverage is thin (496 requested / 476 completed over 3 days versus Claude's thousands per hour); Codex turn.started events lack zellij_pane_id in the data keys seen.

A client reading the bus must not mutate it: connecting with nats-py appears in /connz (a 'waybill-recon-readonly' connection was opened and closed during this recon); creating consumers (even ephemeral) alters server state and was avoided.

memory-state.summary: For one prompt on this machine, the memory/context/state fan-out is highly recorder-friendly, and nearly every hop can be keyed by the native session id. Chain, measured for bdbdba89 (UserPromptSubmit, 03:53:25.284Z): hub receives at .284 and selects all 9 handlers; async rows (publisher, hindsight-turn, nanoleaf, orca-status) start in parallel at .408; the bloodbank-publisher (inside agent-hooks) folds the turn into ASM Redis at .501 (working edge); sync rows then run serially by `order` - skill-reminder (.408-.540), crank-tag (skipped), hindsight-recall (.634-26.087, 442ms, one `hindsight memory recall` CLI subprocess per bank, server-side audit row .716-.075), codegraph-prompt (skipped: binary not on hub PATH), hub-selftest - so the prompt waits about 0.9s. Hindsight writes are NOT per-prompt: the ask is only buffered in a per-session JSON file (~/.local/state/33god/hook-hub/capture/<cli>-<session>.json); the turn (ask+final answer+edited paths) is buffered at Stop; the single append-mode document `session-<cli>-<session>` is POSTed to Hindsight async only when buffer >= 9000 chars, at SessionEnd, or after 2h idle via the sweeper. After that the server runs batch_retain (~12s) -> consolidation (~60-110s, creates observations, refreshes mental models) -> sometimes graph_maintenance, and mental models refresh separately at most every 6h; all on glm-5.3-flash via the hindsight-litellm router (aliases hindsight-retain/consolidation/query/refresh with free/OpenRouter/auto fallback rungs). Evidence that survives locally: hook-hub receipts.sqlite3 (4 days, payload-free), the per-session Hindsight journal (~/.agents/journal/sessions/<cli>-<session>.jsonl, which carries invocation_id), the capture state file, and the ASM transition stream/log. The Hindsight server audit log holds the full recall query and the exact memories returned, which is the only place the injected context can be reconstructed. Several silent gaps found: claude-notify symlink is broken (no sound/notification at all), codegraph-prompt and half of code-review-graph never run because the hub's PATH excludes mise shims and ~/.local/bin, and the hindsight-journal LOG.md always reports 0 retains.

model-transcripts.slice: Vendor side: what Claude Code, Codex CLI and Codex Desktop do with a prompt between the hooks, and where each step is recorded. Covers model routing through the AutomaticAI gateway, Claude and Codex transcripts, Desktop vs CLI, and the correlation joins.
model-transcripts.summary:
Claude Code, Codex CLI and Codex Desktop all send inference through the AutomaticAI gateway (aai-gateway, https://api.automaticai.io), not directly to Anthropic or OpenAI. The `claude()` shell function injects ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and a gateway token through `op run`. This process confirmed it: env has ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.automaticai.io and ANTHROPIC_MODEL=automaticai/auto/orchestrator. Codex uses model_provider=automaticai (`/v1/responses`, token from `op read`). OPENAI_BASE_URL=127.0.0.1:4001 is dead (no listener) and the `litellm` provider is not the active one. Nothing local is called LiteLLM on the hot path. jev-litellm is only the auto-router's classifier.

Every gateway request leaves a row in NewAPI's `logs` table, with `other` carrying the session id, the auto-router decision, `frt` (first-response ms) and `stream_status`. Four routes reach it:
- Candystore event `bloodbank.llm.usage.recorded` carries `data.session_id`, route, native model, tokens, TTFT and a coarse latency.
- An admin PAT (`op://DeLoSecrets/l2wcxoseb33kpdsfijbpitu73u/credential`) can GET `/api/log/` by `request_id`, time window, `token_name` or `model_name`.
- `/api/automaticai/traces/{request_id}` returns the router steps and the upstream attempts (fallback hops). It is kept for three 06:00-ET windows.
- A direct Postgres read-only role exists, but I did not use it.

Verified end to end:
- A Claude Code transcript assistant message joined to its gateway row by session id, token counts and time (request id 202611160355130300634458268d9d65BRZZsba, ledger id 947543, matches transcript requestRef 00dd27e4-975a-4078-864d-e870942a8027).
- A Codex rollout `token_usage_record` joined to its gateway row the same way.

The Claude transcript is unusually rich. It holds:
- the typed user entry with promptId and turnPosition;
- an `api-request`, `api-request-shape` and `api-request-blob` triple per model call: params, betas, effort, and content hashes of the request;
- one assistant entry per content block, with `requestRef`, `requestedModel` (the gateway route name) and `message.model` (the native model);
- tool_use / tool_result pairs;
- `hook_success` attachments keyed by toolUseID;
- one merged `hook_additional_context` attachment that contains the injected `hindsight:recall` text (verified at jsonl line 19);
- Stop `stop_hook_summary` and `turn_duration` system entries;
- subagent sidechains under `<session>/subagents/workflows/<wf>/agent-*.jsonl`. These reuse the parent sessionId and promptId.

The Codex rollout has `session_meta` (originator/source/cli_version), `turn_context`, `task_started`, `task_complete` (with duration_ms and time_to_first_token_ms), `token_usage_record` (response_id plus per-call usage), `function_call*` items and `item_completed`. Hook-injected context lands as role=developer messages. `thread_history_1.sqlite`.`thread_turns` stores per-turn rollout byte offsets. I verified that these slice a turn exactly: ordinals 1..320, task_started to task_complete.

Codex Desktop uses the same `~/.codex` home and config (the launcher defaults CODEX_HOME to ~/.codex). Its hooks do fire: Desktop session 01a19e88-7c8a-7d21-a973-149d2e30ff3d has SessionStart, 2 turn.started and 25 tool events in Candystore, with payload.transcript_path. The hook payload does not say Desktop. The only discriminators are the rollout `session_meta.originator` (`codex_work_desktop`, older `Codex Desktop`) with source `vscode`, and `state_5.sqlite` threads.originator. The gateway sees the same `aai:codex:*` token for Desktop and CLI.

Gaps and cautions:
- Hook-hub receipts are kept only about 4 days, from 2026-11-12T18:22Z, 102,552 rows. They cannot be filtered by session (the filter is ignored), so page and filter client-side.
- The Claude transcript has no gateway request_id, so that join is by session, token counts and time.
- The gateway records the Claude session id but not the subagent agent id, so subagent requests share the parent session.
- Background haiku-slot calls such as ai-title reach the gateway with no `api-request` entry in the transcript.

surprises: Claude Code here never talks to Anthropic directly: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is injected by the `claude()` launcher through `op run`, and ~/.claude/settings.json env does not contain it. Nothing LiteLLM-shaped is on the hot path. OPENAI_BASE_URL=127.0.0.1:4001 is a dead leftover (no listener), and `jev-litellm` is only the router's classifier.

The Claude transcript is a near-complete client-side flight recorder. api-request/api-request-blob/api-request-shape entries hold exact params, betas, effort, cache breakpoints and content-hashed bodies for every main-thread call. Hook-injected context is recorded, but only as ONE merged `hook_additional_context` string for UserPromptSubmit, with no per-handler split and no hook_success for that event.
Claude splits a single API response across several assistant entries (one per content block) and repeats the full usage on each. Summing usage per entry overcounts; dedupe on requestRef/message.id.
Background haiku-slot calls such as ai-title hit the gateway (and Candystore) but leave no api-request entry in the transcript, so transcript-only token accounting undercounts.
A gateway usage event's correlationid is its own id, so `/sessions/{sid}` and `?q=<session>` miss all gateway requests. Gateway usage must be fetched by time window and filtered on data.session_id.

Codex persists the user message AFTER the UserPromptSubmit hooks finish (receipt 00:53:25.889Z, last handler done 00:53:26.722Z, user item 00:53:26.736Z), then immediately appends the hook-injected developer message. Claude does the opposite: the user entry is written first (25.260Z) and the additionalContext attachment later (26.199Z).

Codex's Candystore turn_id is the native UUIDv7 and matches rollout turn_context, token_usage_record and thread_turns exactly. Claude's turn_id is a synthetic `<session>:turn:N` that is not in the transcript and must be mapped via turnPosition.turnIndex.
thread_history_1.sqlite `thread_turns` has rollout byte offsets that slice a turn out of a rollout exactly (verified), so no JSONL scanning is needed for Codex.

Codex Desktop shares everything with the CLI (CODEX_HOME=~/.codex, hooks.json, gateway token), and its hooks do fire. A Desktop turn is distinguishable only via rollout session_meta.originator (codex_work_desktop, older 'Codex Desktop') or threads.originator. source=vscode alone misleads, because codex-tui and hermes rows also use it. The hook payload and the gateway carry no originator.

Claude's transcript for this session is under ~/.claude/projects/-home-delorenj-code-33GOD/ (launch dir) even though the session's cwd is 33god-platform, so a recorder must glob by session id rather than derive the slug from the working directory.

Codex hooks trust entries in config.toml ([hooks.state."~/.codex/hooks.json:user_prompt_submit:3:0"] etc.) reference group indices that do not exist in the current hooks.json (UserPromptSubmit has groups 0-1), so the trust state looks stale, yet the hooks fire (receipts and Candystore prove it). I cannot infer hook trust from config.toml alone.

hook-hub receipts silently ignore a `session_id` query filter and retain only about 4 days (102,552 rows from 2026-11-12T18:22Z).
Gateway latency_ms is quantized to whole seconds and occurred_at is completion time; usage events appear about 7s after the request, so a live recorder must wait before the final join.

Auto-router traces (steps + upstream attempts = fallback hops) are the only place the fallback chain is recorded, and they expire after three 06:00-ET windows. A recorder that wants fallback hops must copy the trace at capture time.

I ran two real prompts from /tmp. `claude -p` ran 04:00:37.387Z to 04:00:41.678Z, session 956a26e9-3f7f-4226-9491-8590d87cc90e. `codex exec` ran 04:06:19.036Z to 04:06:26.514Z, session 01a1e288-d177-7eb3-a080-751c3ec47af9. Both fired the full native hook chain into hook-hub: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and SessionEnd. No tools ran, so PreToolUse and PostToolUse never fired. The order of cause and effect for one prompt is:
1. The CLI boots and spawns its MCP servers.
2. The Orca shim runs, then bb-hook sends to the hook-hub socket.
3. hook-hub writes a receipt invocation and runs the sync handlers: Hindsight briefing/recall in bank `general` (the /tmp fallback), candystore-context (which always fails), and skips for skill-reminder/codegraph/notebook.
4. The bloodbank-publisher handler runs async. It does agent-hooks publish.py, sends a NATS JetStream BLOODBANK_EVENTS event, then Candystore ingests it within 7-37 ms. The ASM fold in Redis sends a synthetic transition invocation back to hook-hub, which runs asm-log into transitions.log.
5. The hook-hub outbox emits bloodbank.agent.hook.updated, one per invocation.
6. The model call goes through the AutomaticAI gateway, which emits llm.usage.recorded and llm.allowance.observed about 1.5 s after the call.
7. On turn.completed, turn-enricher classifies the turn with the Jev gate as noise.
8. On session.ended, the enricher rolls up the session and emits report.session.completed. Candystore then dead-letters it as malformed.
9. ntfy-router pushes or rate-limits each lifecycle event.

The cause chain on the bus is explicit: session.started has id = session_id, and each later event's causationid is the previous event's id. Joining the invocation, the CloudEvent and the gateway usage record needs session_id plus time. codex exec also spawned a hidden second session, the Codex memories "Phase 2 Consolidation" agent (01a1e288-d2f7-...). It ran its own complete hook chain and events, made no gateway call and failed.

A separate mutable `clock.t` is read per-frame outside React (HOURS_PER_SEC=2, START_HOUR=8) so sim time does not re-render. Note = {id, kind 'post'|'env', headline, from, noteId, barcode, seq, bornH, col, viaDesk, subject, hatch, heldBy, tries, retryAt, readBy[]}. Flyer = {look, from, to, t0, dur, arc, hold}; Puff = {at, text, t0, life, tone}. The `ui` helper object (openStation/openBulb/overview/top/fly) mutates the store and bumps focus.nonce to retrigger the camera. The sim scheduler (sim.ts) is imperative: a sorted `jobs` array + later(delay, fn), advanced by step(realDt) from <Sim/>'s useFrame; step returns early only on paused||intro. It is NOT deterministic and cannot be scrubbed. For Waybill: add mode 'waybill' plus {waybill: Waybill|null, wbT (ms playhead), wbPlaying, wbRate, wbSel (span id)}. Drive visuals as a pure function of wbT (derive 'active spans at t') rather than via later(), so scrubbing and replay are exact.

BASE_FOV 42; top view uses TOP_FOV 5 looking nearly straight down; when a panel is open a setViewOffset shifts the frame so the subject is not under the card. viewAt(p, frame=16) is exported and used by the map to build a view. WheelNav (scroll up = top view, scroll down = dive toward cursor) is disabled in tour mode. FogFollow pushes fog back as the camera rises. factory.sim_coexistence: The live sim and tour coexist today: Sim.step only early-returns on paused||intro, so the sim keeps spawning parcels (1.1-2.1s), ticks (5-7s), crew jobs (4.5-7s), batches of 10 (28-36s), audio-trace envelopes (3-5s) during a tour; tour.start() forces speed 1, unpaused, dock open; body.tour-on CSS hides .tick, .parcel-tag, .tag-teal, .puff, .tag-red; StationLabels and WheelNav are disabled in tour mode. Sim rules to be aware of: archive tears copies (8% dupe -> turned away), control tears copies, rules react to 'invocation completed', cataloguer reacts to 'session ended' with a summary post that has no from/barcode, planner reacts to 'tick fired' with a clock envelope 55% of the time; scrapers fire at 7d front / 1d back; seed() pre-ages 46 front notes and 6 grey back envelopes. For Waybill the choice is: (1) pause the sim and hide ambient notes (clean causal view), or (2) leave ambient traffic as faded background context. Recommended: in waybill mode set paused:true and give Waybill its own deterministic entity layer (hero + fan-out ghosts + flyers computed from wbT); optionally allow a 'Live belt' toggle later. Don't route Waybill through later() since it cannot be scrubbed. Waybill hero objects must not be inspectable Notes in useWorld.notes unless pinned to the belt deliberately, to avoid polluting the sim's stats and readers.

factory.data_loading: Three loaders. (1) Same-origin: put dumps in sandbox/public/waybills/*.json; Vite copies them to /sandbox/waybills/ and fetch(`${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}waybills/x.json`) works, the same pattern as voice.ts reading relative voice/manifest.json. Note public/voice is gitignored; waybills can be committed samples or also gitignored. (2) ?waybill=<absolute url>: verified s3.delo.sh (MinIO) echoes any Origin (access-control-allow-origin: <origin>, allow-credentials true, vary: Origin) and answers preflight 204 with allow-methods GET, so https://manual.delo.sh and http://localhost:5173 can fetch published dumps; use fetch(url,{credentials:'omit',cache:'no-cache'}). publish.py sets Content-Type via mimetypes (application/json) and Cache-Control 'no-cache, no-transform', so dumps publish to https://s3.delo.sh/projects/<project>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<name>/ via the artifacts skill. (3) Local file: drag-and-drop and <input type=file> using FileReader/File.text(), no network. Validate `version`; reject unknown major; tolerate unknown span kinds by falling back to a generic kiosk. Dumps should be payload-light (hook-hub receipts are payload-free by design), so large bodies live behind payloadRef URLs fetched lazily by the inspector.
factory.build_deploy: Build: `npm run build` = `tsc --noEmit && vite build` (TypeScript 7 native, typecheck ~0.19s); mise task `build` = `npm ci && npm run build`; deploy == build. Vite base '/sandbox/', outDir ../books/sandbox with emptyOutDir true, chunkSizeWarningLimit 2000. Output is a single JS chunk of about 1.5 MB (about 10 MB total with voice files). manual/books/.gitignore ignores sandbox/, so the bundle is never committed. It is live-served: ~/docker/stacks/websites/manual/compose.yml runs nginx:alpine with manual/books bind-mounted read-only behind Traefik at manual.delo.sh with the default nginx config (no CORS, no cache headers). Therefore running the build replaces the live site instantly (emptyOutDir wipes it first, with a brief window of 404s). Dev: vite dev server (port 5173). Voice assets are generated by tools/voice (render via vox.delo.sh into public/voice, gitignored), tour lines are not voiced. For Waybill dumps, prefer MinIO URLs so republishing a dump never needs a site rebuild.
risks: Live-served build: `npm run build` empties and rewrites ../books/sandbox, which nginx serves read-only immediately, so a failed or partial build takes manual.delo.sh/sandbox/ down. Build to a temp outDir and swap, or run on a branch/preview first.

Sim is non-deterministic (Math.random, mutable clock.t, later() queue) and has no scrubbing; Waybill must not be built on it. A pure function of wbT is required for scrub and replay, which means a second entity layer.

drei <Html> labels are DOM nodes with per-frame transforms; the budget is about 60 and each Tag raycasts the belt every 3rd frame. Auto-placed kiosks for ~25 unmapped components plus per-span tags can blow that budget; use a shared label pool or show tags only for active spans.
Single 1.5 MB JS chunk; adding a waterfall, schema validation, and a lot of new props grows it. chunkSizeWarningLimit is already 2000.

Phone layout: panels become bottom sheets at <=720px, and .dialogue is z41/.notebook z39; a waterfall at the bottom competes with the controls and cards. Portrait overview uses a different view (pos [38,30,58]) and tours scale views by portraitK 1.6, so a waybill needs a collapsed mini-waterfall for portrait.
TypeScript 7.0.2 is the native Go port (preview-era): plugin/API differences can break tooling (eslint typescript-parser, vite plugins) if added.

Anchors and layout coordinates are hand-authored and duplicated across layout.ts, content.ts, domains.ts, sets.ts and map/graph.ts (map warns in dev only if a PART moves); moving a station silently desynchronizes tour anchors, camera views and map lanes. Placing new stations must add to all of them, or be centralised.
Map lanes are authored: a recorded trace that traverses an edge with no authored lane (e.g. hook-hub -> asm, hook-hub -> hindsight direct) needs generated lanes or the map overlay will not light up.

Fidelity drift: registry has 90 components but the Factory models ~16; metaphors (e.g. Hindsight as a library, 'doorbell vs registered publish') hide real semantics. Unmapped spans may mislead if they all collapse onto one kiosk. Show real component name in the tag always (canon: every label is a real 33GOD name).

Privacy: a prompt dump can contain prompt text, file paths, and session ids; receipts are payload-free by design, but Waybill publishing to the public MinIO (s3.delo.sh anonymous-read) would expose content. Redact by default, hash prompt text, and gate payloadRef.

Receipts journal does not capture non-hook side effects (NATS PubAck/seq, Dapr consume deliveries, Candystore ingest, Hindsight retain, Redis transitions, LLM calls); a faithful 'every side effect' dump needs a tap on those systems (bloodbank subscriber on bloodbank.> and invocation-id/correlationid joins), not only receipts.sqlite3.

Time-base mismatch: sim time is 2 sim-hours/sec; waybill spans are real ms (a prompt turn is ~hundreds of ms for hooks to minutes for enrichment). Need an independent playhead and per-span minimum display time/easing so 2 ms handlers are visible.
Tour lines are unvoiced and the tour copy is hard-coded; there is no existing narration path for generated text. Waybill captions will be templated text only.
surprises: The sim keeps running during the tour (Sim.step only stops on paused||intro); tour.start() just forces speed 1/unpaused/dock open and CSS hides some tags.

hook-hub's receipts.sqlite3 (invocations, executions with duration_ms/started_at/finished_at/event_id/publish_status, receipt_events, observation_outbox) is payload-free and already nearly the waterfall Waybill needs; no new recorder is required for the hook-hub half.
